purpose: Population-weighted baseline health/school accessibility.
processing_method: Build arterial graph; class x surface x width speeds; nearest facility/population snapping; multi-source Dijkstra; population weighting.
key_results: Arterial health 60min ranges 35.91% Ethiopia to 90.69% Philippines; corrected noded networks are higher.
limitations: Arterial-only version is a lower-bound sensitivity.

purpose: Measure simultaneous dependence on unpaved roads.
processing_method: Remove all unpaved arterial edges and rerun access.
key_results: Large losses in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, and Bangladesh.
limitations: Artificial stress test, not realistic simultaneous failure.

purpose: Estimate one recent flood footprint per country.
processing_method: Representative-point road-footprint match; remove affected unpaved and halve affected paved/unknown speed.
key_results: Pakistan and Mozambique show largest losses.
limitations: Events differ by country and are not probabilistic.

purpose: Quantify within-country heterogeneity across real flood/cyclone footprints on both arterial and corrected national graphs.
processing_method: Apply 18 curated event footprints to topology-noded national graphs; mark representative road points; compute direct surface-aware health/education access; merge corrected baseline and positive loss.
key_results: Corrected losses range from near zero to 26.61 pp. Pakistan 2025 health loss is 21.53 pp and Mozambique 2025 health loss is 26.61 pp; several small footprints are near zero.
limitations: Convenience sample and equal event weighting are not an annual expected-loss model.

purpose: Compare service-specific sensitivity.
processing_method: Run health and school models on identical inputs.
key_results: Health and school access/disruption differ systematically.
limitations: Facility completeness differs by service.

purpose: Test value of surface and width.
processing_method: Compare M1 class-only, M2 class+surface, M3 class+surface+width.
key_results: Mozambique M1 health 77.88% vs M3 72.86%; Pakistan M1 46.85% vs M3 43.95%.
limitations: Needs noded-network rerun for final paper.

purpose: Compare OSM surface tags and Planet predictions on arterial and corrected topology-noded national graphs.
processing_method: Compare known surface share and accessibility under Planet priority, OSM tags and OSM-plus-Planet fill; use 2024 surfaces, corrected graphs and registry-union facilities.
key_results: Corrected Planet-known share exceeds OSM by 1.5-13.0 length-percentage points. OSM-only lowers baseline access by up to 2.51 pp (Ethiopia education), 2.32 pp (Pakistan education) and 1.16 pp (Kenya health).
limitations: OSM local-road surfaces are held at current extraction; source-priority inheritance can assign conflicting labels deterministically.

purpose: Assess disruption-rule sensitivity.
processing_method: Compare all-remove, all-slow, surface-aware, and surface-only rules.
key_results: Mozambique health loss -35.67 all-remove, -9.01 all-slow, -15.80 surface-aware pp.
limitations: Direct flood rule underestimates observed restrictions.

purpose: Quantify parameter uncertainty.
processing_method: Vary class speed, surface, width, and hazard deceleration; compute empirical intervals.
key_results: Mozambique health baseline interval 8.67 pp; Pakistan hazard deceleration 6.43 pp.
limitations: Assumption intervals, not statistical confidence intervals.

purpose: Test snapping, MAUP, hazard matching, and last mile.
processing_method: Vary facility/population snapping, aggregation resolution, footprint matching, and last-mile speed.
key_results: 0.05-degree aggregation lowers 60min access 24.26 pp on average; last mile lowers 9.20 pp.
limitations: Noded networks reduce but do not eliminate local access uncertainty.

purpose: Compare with independent city/RAI products.
processing_method: Sample Weiss raster at WorldPop cells; compare national and cell summaries with model and SDG RAI.
key_results: Mean travel Spearman: health 0.714, school 0.679; threshold correlations weak.
limitations: City access differs from health/school access; Sun/CPAS unavailable.

purpose: Compare corrected-model road travel times with independent routing engines.
processing_method: Sample population cells across population strata; route from nearest main-facility node to the cell node with public OSRM; benchmark model Dijkstra duration and a snap/next-zero-filtered robust subset.
key_results: Expanded validation has 553 successful routes: Pearson 0.814, Spearman 0.938, MAE 37.59 min, median model/OSRM ratio 1.304; robust subset n=181 has Pearson 0.867, Spearman 0.960, MAE 17.43 min, ratio 1.277.
limitations: Public OSRM is not ground truth; Google/ORS are unavailable; snapping, endpoint definition and public-network differences affect absolute duration.

purpose: Validate observed blockages and Cyclone Idai rules.
processing_method: Match observed points/lines to networks; validate road status against flood raster and surface; test flood-buffer rules.
key_results: Only 1/32 blockage points within 100m of arterial roads; South Sofala noded network matches 24/24 within 25m. Flood5km OR unpaved: precision 82.28%, recall 70.26%, F1 0.758.
limitations: Single-event calibration; WFP live endpoint unavailable; archive snapshot used.

experiment: Facility validation and corrected facility model
purpose: Audit OSM facilities and rerun with registries.
processing_method: Nearest-match registries to OSM; rerun arterial and noded accessibility using OSM, registry, and union facilities.
key_results: Noded corrected access: Ethiopia health 52.45% to 93.20%; Bangladesh school 93.77% to 97.30%; Mozambique health 75.53% to 84.35%.
limitations: Registry scope/year differs; Pakistan/Kenya health and Colombia education remain count-only.

purpose: Compare urban/rural access.
processing_method: Classify 1km WorldPop cells using GHS-SMOD and calculate access by urban/rural group.
key_results: Kenya baseline health gap 20.00 pp; Mozambique school gap 35.30 pp.
limitations: Needs noded rerun.

purpose: Relate access to SHDI/poverty and diagnose graph artifacts.
processing_method: Assign cells to GDL regions; calculate SHDI correlations; compare arterial and noded Mozambique.
key_results: Mozambique SHDI-health correlation shifts -0.509 arterial to +0.390 noded; school +0.254 to +0.821.
limitations: Only Mozambique corrected; national poverty is not spatial.

purpose: Quantify travel-time inequality.
processing_method: Calculate Gini/concentration indices and density-quintile access.
key_results: School Gini often high; flood-added travel concentrates in lower-density cells.
limitations: Density is an imperfect socioeconomic proxy.

purpose: Identify high-impact roads.
processing_method: Population-weight path usage; remove top 1/5/10% edges and compare random removal.
key_results: Top 1% medical roads cause 5-7 pp losses; top 10% reaches 24-29 pp.
limitations: Arterial-only; noded rankings may differ.

experiment: Restoration priority and noded South Sofala
purpose: Rank post-flood restoration.
processing_method: Restore ranked affected edges; compare population dependency, hazard exposure, random, shortest length.
key_results: South Sofala restoring 10% by population dependency: health +9.28 pp, school +4.60 pp.
limitations: Static rankings; length proxy cost.

experiment: Paving upgrades and noded South Sofala
purpose: Simulate paving investments.
processing_method: Upgrade selected unpaved edges to paved speed; flooded upgraded roads slow instead of closing.
key_results: South Sofala 10% paving: hazard health +3.68 pp; baseline health +3.28 pp.
limitations: Length-only cost; no construction feasibility.

experiment: Budget optimization and noded South Sofala
purpose: Select roads under length budgets.
processing_method: Greedy selection under 1/5/10% length budgets; compare population, exposure, random, length.
key_results: South Sofala 10% budget hazard health +3.10 pp exposure-first vs +0.86 pp random.
limitations: Greedy heuristic, not exact optimisation.

purpose: Jointly sample model parameters.
processing_method: Sample speed, surface, unknown assignment, width, hazard deceleration; 20 draws per country.
key_results: Pakistan school hazard interval 7.11 pp; Mozambique school 6.27 pp.
limitations: No population/facility/event/topology uncertainty.

purpose: Test alternative assumptions for roads whose surface remains unknown, including on corrected national graphs.
processing_method: Compare current slow, as-paved, as-unpaved, no-penalty, class mean and random allocations with independent edge attributes for each rule.
key_results: Across 17 corrected country-service cases, hazard access changes on average +1.81 pp as-paved, -9.55 pp as-unpaved and about -6.6 pp under random allocation; Pakistan hazard health can fall 41.55 pp if all unknowns are unpaved.
limitations: Extreme as-unpaved is a stress test, not an equally likely scenario; random rules condition only on road class.

experiment: Network integrity and noded country networks
purpose: Assess network completeness and build corrected graphs.
processing_method: Download HOT roads; filter motorable classes; shapely union_all Planet+OSM lines; inherit nearest-source attributes; build baseline/hazard graphs.
key_results: Baseline health gains: PAK +47.66, ETH +25.31, KEN +23.25, BGD +20.60, MOZ +19.98, COL +6.26, PHL +0.83 pp.
limitations: Derived caches are large; native OSM node/way graphs preferable.

purpose: Extend beyond seven countries.
processing_method: Not executed.
key_results: No result.
limitations: Requires comparable multi-country inputs and compute.

purpose: Compare 2020 and 2024 Planet surface labels on corrected topology-noded national graphs.
processing_method: Update Planet-assigned noded segments from DL_road_class_2020 to DL_road_class_2024; hold OSM local surfaces, width, facilities, population and hazard footprint constant; compute baseline and surface-aware access.
key_results: Pakistan health hazard access improves +4.68 pp and education +4.04 pp; Mozambique health hazard +3.07 pp; Kenya health hazard +1.29 pp. Baseline changes are smaller.
limitations: No 2016 class on corrected cache; OSM local-road surface dynamics are unavailable.

purpose: Project future hazards.
processing_method: Not executed.
key_results: No result.
limitations: Requires probabilistic future flood/cyclone projections.

purpose: Reproduce original global pavedness analysis.
processing_method: Read aggregate grid; calculate pavedness and unknown share; merge boundaries; make maps/tables.
key_results: 2024 length-weighted pavedness: total 93.76%, urban 99.49%, rural 92.97%.
limitations: Uses aggregate grid, not raw per-road data.

purpose: Test service-access idea.
processing_method: Build road graph and baseline/no-unpaved/flood scenarios.
key_results: Baseline health 73.87%; no-unpaved 63.54%; flood 73.72%.
limitations: Proof of concept with small flood impact.

purpose: Combine corrected topology and registry facilities.
processing_method: Use national noded graphs and alternate OSM/registry/union facility sources.
key_results: Ethiopia health 93.20%; Bangladesh school 97.30%; Mozambique health 84.35% baseline with union facilities.
limitations: Completed only for ETH, BGD, MOZ.

purpose: Rerun core experiments 6, 8, 15, and 17 on the final topology-noded, registry-corrected model.
processing_method: Build M1/M2/M3 graphs on noded caches; use registry-union facilities where available; run direct hazard-rule ablation; classify urban/rural with GHS-SMOD; compute corrected Gini and density-quintile summaries.
key_results: Ignoring surface/width still overstates access; Ethiopia health M1 61.85% versus M3 50.08% under OSM facilities, while registry union gives M1 95.56% versus M3 92.41%.
limitations: Registry unions exist only for ETH health, BGD education, and MOZ health; other services remain OSM-only.

purpose: Test direct versus true spatial-buffer disruption rules on the corrected model.
processing_method: Rasterize each flood footprint at 250 m in EPSG:3857; apply Euclidean distance transform; mark road representative points within 5 km; compare direct, buffer-remove, buffer-OR-unpaved, and buffer-surface-aware rules.
key_results: Buffer5 surface-aware differs modestly from direct surface-aware (for example, Mozambique registry health 55.10% direct versus 54.60% buffer), while buffer5-remove-all and buffer5-OR-unpaved are much more conservative.
limitations: Buffer proximity is not evidence of road inundation; 250 m raster approximation; rules are robustness checks rather than the main model.

purpose: Benchmark corrected-model road travel times against independent public OSRM driving durations, including the expanded 553-route sample.
processing_method: Stratify population-cell samples; route nearest main-facility node to cell node; compare OSRM duration with corrected Dijkstra time; report all-route and snap-filtered robust metrics.
key_results: Expanded all-route Pearson 0.814, Spearman 0.938, MAE 37.59 min, median ratio 1.304. Robust subset Pearson 0.867, Spearman 0.960, MAE 17.43 min, median ratio 1.277.
limitations: Public OSRM is a benchmark, not ground truth; route sample remains modest and destination snapping is often large.

purpose: Provide a second independent event test of hazard/rule spatial overlap using Copernicus road damage status.
processing_method: Label Copernicus restricted/damaged roads as positives; test direct and buffer-distance event rules; separately match Copernicus lines to Nepal Planet surface within 500 m.
key_results: Direct observed-event intersection precision 91.01%, recall 86.43%, F1 0.887. Planet surface subset n=987: direct F1 0.887; direct OR unpaved F1 0.850; Planet unpaved-only F1 0.157.
limitations: Assessment subset is not population-representative; event polygons denote mass movement; Planet-unpaved independent gain is limited in this event.

purpose: Rerun within-country SHDI/access associations on the corrected model for all seven countries.
processing_method: Chunk corrected 1 km cell travel-time files; assign each cell to nearest GDL region; aggregate population-weighted baseline/hazard access; merge SHDI 2020; calculate country-service correlations.
key_results: Corrected SHDI-access correlations are mostly positive. Examples: Mozambique education baseline weighted Pearson 0.832; Kenya health 0.770; Mozambique health 0.699; Pakistan education 0.675.
limitations: Regional ecological associations are not causal; poverty maps remain unavailable; Philippines education remains negative at -0.279.

purpose: Produce paper-ready corrected health/school baseline and hazard-loss maps.
processing_method: Merge corrected GDL-region access summaries with GDL boundaries; plot seven-country facets for health/school baseline and hazard loss; export GPKG layers.
key_results: Four publication-style PNG maps and two GPKG layers for corrected health and school access.
limitations: GDL-region choropleths are coarser than 1 km cell results and should be interpreted with MAUP caution.

purpose: Test unknown-road surface assumptions on a full topology-noded national network after repairing edge-attribute contamination.
processing_method: Compare current slow, as-paved, as-unpaved, no-penalty, class-mean and three random assignments using independent edge dictionaries for each rule.
key_results: Relative to current slow, hazard health access changes +0.51 pp as-paved, -1.71 pp as-unpaved, and -0.28 to -0.33 pp across random seeds; hazard education changes +0.01, -0.55, and -0.18 to -0.19 pp.
limitations: Historical pilot; superseded by the all-country S16 rerun.

purpose: Decompose Ethiopia health facility types and test three large 2023 flood-event footprints on the corrected national graph.
processing_method: Evaluate OSM and registry facility type subsets under baseline/direct hazard; mark three WFP strong-event footprints and compare surface-aware, all-remove and all-slow rules.
key_results: Registry primary care reaches 92.26% baseline versus 50.08% with OSM hospital/clinic. Strong-event health losses reach -24.45 pp (2023-11-14 surface-aware) and -48.85 pp (2023-11-21 surface-aware) from the 92.26% baseline.
limitations: Facility scopes differ by type/year; three events are selected strong footprints rather than a probability sample.

purpose: Repair corrected Gini sign, enforce positive hazard-loss convention, integrate expanded OSRM, and regenerate canonical maps and paper-ready tables.
processing_method: Correct weighted-Gini sign, define hazard loss as baseline minus hazard, use expanded OSRM summary, clip map losses at zero, make GDL geometries valid, and regenerate outputs/figures.
key_results: Corrected baseline Gini values are now non-negative (reachable mean 0.606); all main hazard losses are non-negative; expanded OSRM is the canonical routing benchmark.
limitations: Derived reconciliation does not add new independent validation data.

purpose: Test whether Planet unpaved surface independently predicts Copernicus road damage in the Nepal 2026 event.
processing_method: Match Copernicus transportation lines to Nepal Planet roads within 500 m and calculate precision/recall/F1 for direct event intersection, direct OR Planet-unpaved, and Planet-unpaved-only rules.
key_results: n=987 matched lines. Direct event intersection F1 0.887; direct OR Planet-unpaved F1 0.850; Planet-unpaved-only precision 45.54%, recall 9.47%, F1 0.157.
limitations: Matched subset may favour well-mapped roads; event process is flash flood/mass movement rather than pure inundation.

purpose: Run 2020/2024 surface transitions on all seven topology-noded national graphs.
processing_method: Build a graph with both year-specific surface labels and travel times; run baseline and surface-aware scenarios with corrected facilities.
key_results: Hazard improvements exceed baseline improvements in Pakistan, Mozambique and Kenya; Pakistan health hazard +4.68 pp and Mozambique health hazard +3.07 pp.
limitations: OSM local surfaces and non-surface inputs are held constant; 2016 remains unavailable.

experiment: Corrected OSM versus Planet surface sensitivity
purpose: Compare Planet priority, OSM tags and OSM-plus-Planet fill on corrected national graphs.
processing_method: Map OSM tags and Planet predictions to noded segments; rebuild source-specific graphs; compare known share, agreement and accessibility.
key_results: Planet-known share exceeds OSM in all seven countries; OSM-only reduces access most in Ethiopia education, Pakistan and Kenya. OSM-plus-Planet fill is not uniformly better than Planet priority because conflicts override Planet labels.
limitations: Current OSM local surfaces and deterministic source-priority attribution limit causal interpretation.

purpose: Rerun unknown-surface sensitivity for all seven corrected national graphs after fixing nested edge contamination.
processing_method: Apply eight unknown-handling rules with independent edge attribute updates; report baseline/hazard access and removed-edge counts.
key_results: Hazard mean changes are +1.81 pp as-paved, -9.55 pp as-unpaved and about -6.6 pp random. Largest stress-test loss is Pakistan health -41.55 pp.
limitations: As-unpaved is a deliberately severe stress test; class/random assumptions do not use imagery or contextual covariates.

purpose: Run the curated 18-event archive on corrected national graphs with official-union facilities.
processing_method: Load each country graph once; spatially join event footprints to road representative points; apply direct surface-aware disruption and merge corrected baseline loss.
key_results: Corrected health losses range from 0 to 26.61 pp; Pakistan 2025 is 21.53 pp and Mozambique 2025 is 26.61 pp, while many small footprints are near zero.
limitations: Convenience event sample; no annual probabilities, protection assumptions or climate projections.

purpose: Test whether a learned model transfers between observed road-status events and improves over hand-designed hazard rules.
processing_method: Combine Idai and Nepal labelled roads; use hazard distance, Planet surface, match distance and interactions; test logistic, balanced logistic and random forest with leave-one-event-out and pooled stratified CV.
key_results: Pooled 5-fold random-forest AUC is 0.931, but leave-one-event-out transfer is poor (for example AUC 0.44 Nepal-to-Idai and 0.48-0.81 Idai-to-Nepal depending model). Simple best rules remain event-specific.
limitations: Only two events; hazard semantics differ; no terrain, hydrology, bridge or rainfall covariates; pooled CV is not spatial transfer evidence.

purpose: Create a pre-specified stratified expansion sample, validate input availability, and progressively build corrected national accessibility models beyond the original seven countries.
processing_method: Pre-specify 30 countries; audit/download Planet roads, WorldPop, OSM facilities and full-road archives; run the 23-country arterial baseline; topology-node Planet+OSM roads for all 23 additions (union/nodal noding, nearest-source attribute inheritance, multi-source Dijkstra) and compute corrected baseline access. Large additions use the tiled memory-bounded runner (1.5-degree tiles with adaptive sub-tiling, tile-local nearest joins, DuckDB node/edge collapse). The tiled runner was validated against the canonical runner on Sri Lanka (access shares within 0.014 pp; noded length within 0.0007%) and Nepal (within 0.049 pp; length within 0.005%). A full data audit then checked input inventory, baseline consistency, population units, the length metric and hazard coverage, and produced corrected variants (count weights, geodesic lengths, no-unpaved and unknown-as-unpaved scenarios) plus an observed-event hazard pilot.
key_results: 30/30 Planet and WorldPop URLs available; 46/46 facility exports available; 23-country arterial baseline complete; all 23 additions have corrected noded baselines (46 country-service rows, up to 31.4M noded segments for India). Local-road correction ranges from -24.65 pp (PNG health) to +73.98 pp (Egypt health); India health rises 77.74% -> 97.48% and India education 55.31% -> 90.36%. Audit: the WorldPop `*_pd_2020_1km.tif` layer is a density raster, so canonical absolute populations are inflated 1.16-1.82x (population-weighted shares move only -0.08 to +0.11 pp); EPSG:3857 segment lengths overstate distance by up to +35% at high latitude, which raises 30-min access by up to +6.90 pp (Kyrgyzstan health) once corrected. Uniform stress tests: removing unpaved roads costs up to 61.60 pp of 60-min access (Tanzania health); unknown-as-unpaved costs up to 4.88 pp (Cambodia health). Observed-event hazard pilot: Viet Nam 2020 cyclone (2 962 km2, 2.56M people, 229 869 affected segments) costs -0.71 pp health 30-min access, Indonesia 2025 Aceh -0.21 pp, India 2015 Chennai/coastal Tamil Nadu (16 087 km2, 4.36M people) -0.04 pp, Nigeria 2022 Yobe 0.00 pp (21 km2 footprint touches no mapped road).
limitations: Expansion baselines use OSM-only facilities and no official registries; hazard footprints exist only for the four pilot additions (the other 19 need UNOSAT/HDX sourcing, see probe_hdx_hazards.py); corrected expansion networks are single Planet+OSM snapshots; corrected access can fall below the arterial-only baseline (PNG health -24.65 pp), so both must always be reported; the density-as-counts and Web-Mercator conventions are inherited from the core pipeline and should be re-run there as well.

purpose: Convert corrected multi-event losses into an explicit empirical annual-frequency and exceedance diagnostic while avoiding an unsupported annual expected-loss claim.
processing_method: Use 2018-2026 annual maxima from the corrected event archive, zero-loss years without archived events, Weibull exceedance positions, and 10,000 bootstrap resamples.
key_results: Mean archived-event annual loss is 3.04 pp for Pakistan health, 3.09 pp for Pakistan education and 2.97 pp for Mozambique health, but bootstrap intervals are wide (Pakistan health 0.24-7.84 pp; Mozambique health 0-8.88 pp).
limitations: Convenience event sample; no representative event probabilities or return-period hazard layers; values must not be called annual expected loss or climate risk.
